reviews.text:
I stopped by Chungmu House to eat flounder mugwort soup, one of the foods I want to eat when spring comes. Spring was over, and I was impatient because I would soon have to move my office.

Without hesitation, I ordered the mugwort soup and sea squirt rice set. As expected, the mugwort was large and the scent was strong, but I still felt relieved at the thought of eating flounder mugwort soup in season this year. And although the scent was strong, the combination of the refreshing flounder broth and mugwort scent was very good.

The sea squirt rice had a nice sea scent and savory taste as it was in season. It tasted good, as if the sharp rice grains were coated with the scent of sesame oil, salted sea squirt, seaweed, and other ingredients, all combining well. Especially since I was eating flounder and mugwort soup in between meals.

It felt like I was forcing myself to eat it, holding on to the end of spring that had passed, like holding on to the pant leg of a girlfriend who had left me, but even so, after eating it, I felt much more at peace with no regrets.

It was a good meal that helped me control my impatience as spring passed faster than expected. I had a good time.

All foods that can be eaten according to Islamic teachings are called halal foods. This essentially means any food that does not fall into the category of haram (or forbidden). In Islam, all food and drinks are halal except those explicitly prohibited in the Quran. Muslims around the world accept the Quran as a book that provides perfect guidance and guidance to humanity, and believe it to be God's final revelation.

God says in the Quran: (translation)
“Eat of the good things I have given you.” (Quran 2:172)
“Eat what is lawful (halal) and healthy (tayib) in this world.” (Quran 2:168)
“O mankind, eat whatever is lawful and good in this world, and do not follow in the footsteps of Satan, for he is a clear enemy to you.” (Quran 2:168)

Although some specific teachings differ, the general view is that food/drinks should not contain pork, alcohol/liquors, poisons, harmful ingredients, or unhygienic elements. All meat must be slaughtered according to methods prescribed by Islamic law, known as Zabihah.

reviews.author: Gourmet Tourist (danzzanaz)
reviews.text:
Bone pork belly restaurant located in Jonggak
Bone pork belly can be ordered for 3 people or more, and if you order, you will understand why.
The meat attached to the large bones is really soft and savory.
Because it is sold after aging, the meat feels much softer than regular raw meat.
They also serve a variety of salted seafood that they marinate themselves, and the compatibility of this salted seafood with meat is really good.
Since the meat is attached to the bone, it has more fat than other parts, so it can be greasy, but the sweet and salty taste of this salted fish completely eliminates that greasiness.
Since they only grill thick types of meat, there is no advantage in eating thin meat at this restaurant.
The stew is expensive at 7,000 won, but the quality compared to the price is very disappointing.
However, if you make a reservation through Naver Reservation, this stew is provided as a service.
Be sure to make a reservation and visit.
If you want to eat delicious meat grilled at Jonggak, I recommend the bone pork belly at Saegyeop Restaurant.

english

A bone pork belly restaurant located in Jonggak, a must-try spot for meat lovers. Bone pork belly is available for orders starting from three people, and once you try it, you'll understand why. They also serve various pickled side dishes, which go perfectly with the meat. As bone pork belly can be fatty compared to other cuts, the sweet and salty taste of the side dishes helps balance out the richness. Only thick cuts of meat are grilled here, so there's no point in ordering thin slices. The stew is on the pricier side at 7,000 won, but it's not worth the price in terms of quality. reviews.text:
I had already finished visiting Myeongdong Gyoza, which is an annual event every winter, and I wanted to try a new restaurant, so I decided to go to Tsuruhashi Fugetsu, which I had remembered from a long time ago.

I didn't expect there to be a wait, but one of my group members used a catch table to wait for 1 hour and 40 minutes. Maybe it was because there were a lot of people in Myeongdong... but it was worth the wait because there was a waiting area inside the store.

The menu is divided into set menus, okonomiyaki, yakisoba, a la carte dishes, alcoholic beverages, and beverages, making it easy to choose by item.

I wondered if they grilled it on an iron plate and brought it to you, but there was an iron plate at each table, which created a nice atmosphere. It has a new and exotic feel, so it looks good for a date.

I visited as a group of three and ordered the premium set for three (58,000 won). Fugetsu Modern Yaki is cooked on an iron plate on the table.

I thought Fugetsu Yakisoba would only come with noodles, but it was good because it had meat, cabbage, and a fried egg. But the downside is that it is too salty and greasy. It feels a bit better when I sprinkle some red pepper powder and green onion powder on it.

The bean sprout roll contains meat and bean sprouts inside, so it is delicious without being greasy. Cheese Donbeiyaki has a chewy texture. Egg rolls can't be tasteless.

They asked me if I wanted to add sauce right before it was finished, but the okonomiyaki sauce mixed with mayonnaise was quite spicy and greasy. The shape of the sauce looks like an eyeball, so I don't like it.

I feel like it would have been more delicious if I had gotten the sauce separately and dipped it to my liking.

The interior of the store consists of a four-person table with iron plates, and you can put clothes inside the chair. I like that there is a divider.

The bathroom was located inside the store, on one floor above, but it was fine except for the fact that there was no hot water. Men and women are separated.

Tsuruhashi Fugetsu also provides coupons, and they say you get one for every 10,000 won. The three of us ate, so I think we'll be able to fill up again in no time.

I quickly got tired of eating all the menu items in the set because they were made with sauces of similar taste, but it has a mysterious charm that makes me think of it again every time I turn around.

So, I'm probably planning to visit again, and then I'll have to eat two okonomiyaki instead of yakisoba. Recommended as a unique Myeongdong restaurant.

reviews.text:
This is a restaurant that my parents have run since the 80s.
It's a place I have very fond memories of, and a place I go to eat at least three or four times a year.
It was closed for about a year around Corona, but after reopening, the quality of fried pork cutlets and service began to worsen.
It is understandable that the size of pork cutlet is getting smaller as the price rises, but it is not uncommon for the batter to come off.
Today, I was told to go up from the 1st floor to the 2nd floor, and they said they were cleaning up, so I told them to order first, then pay... I was taken aback by how much they insisted and yelled at me to pay.
Even though I had paid, they made a loud noise telling me to wait for the table to be cleared before the customer even got up, and instead of properly designating a table, they paid and ordered the food back and forth to another table.
They said it was our food, so they put it down in front of people without even asking who would eat which, and even while they were eating, they were shouting at each other so much, saying things like, “Mr. Manager, the meat is not coming out!”, and shouting over the customers’ heads, making my ears hurt, and I couldn’t tell if the rice was going into their noses or mouths.
No matter how much the servers were punishing and yelling at the customers, I was in a very bad mood. Even though the meal was finishing, chopsticks were being passed around, and people were carrying empty beer glasses, and when I finished eating and started to get dressed, they cleared the table and I was in a hurry to get dressed.
The man in civilian clothes who first showed me around on the first floor didn't look like an employee, but he was standing at the entrance of the store smoking a cigarette...
I won't go back now.
There are many delicious and friendly pork cutlet restaurants.
There is absolutely no need to go here, and there is no reason to go back just for the memories.
